name: James H. Anderson

evidence_summary: Wikipedia stub and UNC notes establish academic standing and fellowships decades after any plausible early-career window. name: Michael W. Allen
milestone_by_age_26: No material founder/product milestone by age 26. Born 1946; worked on Control Data's PLATO system from 1971 (~age 25) as an employee, rising later to R&D director. Founded Authorware in 1984 (~age 38), the defining commercial success.
early_history_summary: Allen earned psychology degrees (BA Cornell College; MA/PhD Ohio State educational psychology). From 1971–1984 he worked on PLATO at Control Data, then founded Authorware (merged into Macromedia, later Adobe). He later founded Allen Interactions and Allen Learning Technologies and authored e-learning guides.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia documents birth year 1946 and Authorware founding in 1984 (age ~38). PLATO work at CDC began at ~25 but was employment, not an independently material founder or breakthrough milestone by the rubric's standard. No second-source evidence of a dated company founding, product launch, or major award by age 26.

name: Alex Zhu
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Born ~1979 (reported as 40 in 2019); graduated Zhejiang University civil engineering in 2000 (~age 21), then product roles at WebEx/SAP. Musical.ly launched 2014 (~age 35); ByteDance acquisition 2017.
early_history_summary: Raised in Anhui, China; Zhejiang University civil engineering B.S. (2000). Product design roles at WebEx and SAP, later eBaoTech in Shanghai with cofounder Luyu Yang. After failed education app Cicada (2013), they launched Musical.ly (2014), which ByteDance acquired (~$1B, 2017) and merged into TikTok.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Anhui upbringing.
evidence_summary: Business Insider (2019) described Zhu as 40 and cited Zhejiang graduation in 2000, implying birth ~1979; Musical.ly launch (2014) was at ~35. Early career was corporate product work, not a dated breakout by 26. Family advantage details are not documented in reviewed sources.

name: Paula Long
milestone_by_age_26: No verified birth year; defining milestone was cofounding EqualLogic in 2001, which she has said was in her 30s. Prior DEC/Bright Tiger/Allaire engineering roles also appear post-college career, not a documented ≤26 breakout.
early_history_summary: Born Methuen, MA; raised Enfield, CT; CS bachelor's from Westfield State. UNIX engineer at DEC, then Bright Tiger (acquired by Allaire) and Iron Stream. Cofounded EqualLogic (2001) with Peter Hayden and Paul Koning; Dell acquired it for $1.4B (2008). Later cofounded DataGravity (CEO).
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Mixergy interviews place EqualLogic founding in 2001 while Long was in her 30s; Dell exit was 2008. Birth year is not published; no multi-source evidence of a material company founding, product, or award by age 26.

name: John Cook
milestone_by_age_26: In 1996 (~age 20), co-created and released Team Fortress, a class-based multiplayer Quake mod that became one of the most-played Quake mods worldwide and led to Valve hiring him and Robin Walker in 1998 (~age 22).
early_history_summary: Grew up in a small Australian town as a childhood friend of Robin Walker; both studied computer science at RMIT. They built Team Fortress in QuakeC for LAN parties, released it via ftp.cdrom.com in August 1996, and deferred/left university as the mod exploded. Valve hired TF Software in 1998; Cook led online/platform work and TF2 development through 2016, later founding Sodium.
primary_leverage_engine: Product / domain insight + peer cofounder execution
secondary_engine: Early specialization / prior reps; platform modding wave
family_context_summary: Small-town Australia (~800 people); fathers played guitar together with Walker's family. Cook has said Walker's IBM-programmer father made computer science visible as a path; Cook's own parental occupations otherwise not detailed.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not clear domain transfer from Cook's own parents; indirect access via childhood friend's programmer father (IBM) who normalized computing careers.
primary_early_advantage_tags: lifelong cofounder Robin Walker, Quake mod community, competitive LAN scene, QuakeC platform wave
evidence_summary: Shacknews oral history and Wikipedia establish Team Fortress release in 1996 and Valve hire in 1998. Birth year ~1976 is estimated from lifelong peer relationship with Robin Walker (Wikipedia: born 1975 or 1976; category 1976 births) and Cook being slightly younger (Shacknews). Even under conservative peer-age bounds, TF and Valve hire fall well under age 26. Family money/networks are not documented; advantage is peer team + mod-platform distribution.
starting_point: Raised in a small Australian town (~800 people) as a childhood friend of Robin Walker; early exposure to board games, home computers, and (via Walker's father) the idea of computer science as a career.
current_position: Left Valve in 2016 after ~18 years; founder of Sodium (post-Valve venture); co-creator of the Team Fortress franchise that continues as a free-to-play Valve title.

trajectory.event: Co-released Team Fortress as a free Quake mod; it rapidly became one of the most-played multiplayer mods online.
Hired by Valve with Robin Walker to bring Team Fortress into the Half-Life ecosystem commercially.
Team Fortress Classic shipped as a free Half-Life mod, bringing TF gameplay to a much larger audience.
Team Fortress 2 launched in The Orange Box, redefining the series with its art direction and class design.
Left Valve after roughly 18 years and founded Sodium.

name: Tandy Trower
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Approximate birth year ~1953 (reported age 57 in Sept 2010). Joined Microsoft in 1981 (~age 28) after Atari product roles (~1980). Major Windows marketing and Microsoft Robotics Studio leadership came later.
early_history_summary: Self-taught programming on TRS-80/Apple II after semiconductor engineering work; software roles at Wicat (1979) and Atari personal computers (~1980), then Microsoft from 1981 for ~28 years (BASIC languages, Windows marketing, Microsoft Agent, Robotics Studio GM). Founded Hoaloha Robotics after leaving Microsoft in 2009.
evidence_summary: Seattle Times/robotics coverage in 2010 listed Trower as 57, implying birth ~1953. Microsoft join date 1981 (~age 28) is corroborated by Wikipedia and his own interviews. No multi-source evidence of a material dated product launch, founding, or field-defining role by age 26.

name: Jeffrey P. Buzen
milestone_by_age_26: No material field-defining milestone by age 26. Born May 28, 1943; Brown ScB 1965, Harvard MS 1966, NIH systems programmer 1967–69 with a 1969 IEEE conference paper (~age 26). Defining Buzen's algorithm work is tied to his 1971 PhD (~age 28) and 1973 paper; BGS Systems founded 1975 (~age 32).
early_history_summary: Brooklyn-born applied mathematician; Brown and Harvard degrees. Early NIH systems programming fed into PhD research on queueing network models of multiprogramming (1971). Lectured at Harvard while at Honeywell; cofounded BGS Systems (BEST/1 performance tools); later NAE member and ACM SIGMETRICS award winner.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Brooklyn birth.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and ACM Ubiquity interview date birth (1943), degrees, and the 1971 dissertation / 1973 algorithm paper that made him famous. An early 1969 IEEE paper at age 26 is training-stage, not the material defining contribution. Company founding and NAE election were well after 26.

name: Tom Dale

Interview says he taught himself Rails in his 'very early 20s' at an Apple Genius Bar, but without birth year age at Ember cannot be confirmed ≤26.
early_history_summary: Self-taught programmer (no CS degree); Apple Genius Bar then rogue-to-corporate MobileMe web work on SproutCore; later Strobe (acquired by Facebook), cofounded Tilde with Yehuda Katz, and co-created Ember.js. Senior staff engineer roles at LinkedIn and later Vercel.
evidence_summary: The New Stack interview and Ember history sources confirm Apple→Strobe→Tilde/Ember path but never state birth year. Strict age≤26 rule requires a dated milestone with verified age; Ember 2011 is potentially early-career but not age-confirmed, so coded ineligible.
